label: Bansal S05: opioid with dementia
title: Ongoing opioid in a person with dementia
statement: Persistent prescription of opioid analgesics to a patient with dementia [64, 65]

source.document: Bansal N, et al. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care. BMC Med 2024;22:5, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x
source.credit: Bansal N, Campbell SM, Lin C-Y, Ashcroft DM, Chen L-C. Development of prescribing indicators related to opioid-related harm in patients with chronic pain in primary care - a modified e-Delphi study. BMC Med 2024;22:5. doi:10.1186/s12916-023-03213-x

plain_summary: Opioids can add to confusion, drowsiness and falls in a person with dementia.

medicine_groups.name: Opioid pain medicines
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, patches and injections used for pain count. Codeine combined with paracetamol counts, for example Panadeine Forte. Targin is oxycodone with naloxone. Count methadone when the product and record support use for pain. Ask for the indication if it is unclear. Exclude methadone and buprenorphine used for opioid dependence. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Count only opioid analgesics used for pain in the source population. If the indication is unknown, report at most a possible finding and ask what the product was used for. Exclude substitution treatment and codeine cough preparations. Physeptone tablets can be used for pain. Opod-D Syrup has both pain and dependence indications. Confirm its use before counting it. Opod-P Liquid, Physeptone Liquid and Biodone Forte are dependence products. Codeine with ibuprofen or aspirin counts when used for pain.

needs_facts.meets: Dementia was present during the opioid course. An unknown answer leaves the finding possible.

options.words: Dementia present during the opioid course
Dementia absent during the opioid course

needs_facts.what: Reason for the opioid course under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only if the product and record leave its purpose unclear and the other evidence fits. Only chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care qualifies for this course. An unknown reason leaves the finding possible.

options.words: Chronic non-cancer pain outside palliative care

needs_facts.what: Duration of the opioid course under review
needs_facts.meets: Ask only when repeat prescriptions span at least three calendar months and the dates, quantities and directions leave continuity uncertain. One continuing course of at least three calendar months qualifies. A shorter course or separate courses do not. If unknown, keep the finding possible.

options.words: Yes, one continuing course of at least three calendar months
No, a shorter course or separate courses

rule_for_models: In a person over 18 at supply whose dementia was present during the opioid course, cite the diagnosis and a Group A opioid supply if more than one prescription for chronic non-cancer pain forms one course of at least three months by documented course dates or by supply dates, quantities and directions. Report no finding for age 18 or younger, dementia ruled out, separate documented short courses, dependence treatment or codeine cough preparations. If the other evidence fits, report only a possible finding and ask about missing age, dementia status, the reason for this opioid course or its duration, whichever is unclear. Ask about duration only if repeat supplies span at least three calendar months and the directions or gaps leave continuity uncertain.
cannot_be_seen: The type and stage of dementia, why the opioid was started, how pain is assessed, and care given by a carer, hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the opioid is still needed, and of non-opioid ways to manage the pain.
